SECONDARY FIX — resources/27-oracle-plsql-to-dbt-trino.md §4.5B 'ROWNUM CANONICAL FORMS — Oracle row-limiting and pagination'. NEW subsection inserted between §4.5A (Iceberg identity column negation) and §4.6 (DML). Establishes the non-negotiable Oracle ROWNUM evaluation order rule (ROWNUM is assigned AS rows are retrieved, BEFORE ORDER BY — verified against docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/ROWNUM-Pseudocolumn.html and Tom Kyte's asktom.oracle.com/Misc/oramag/on-rownum-and-limiting-results.html). 7-row canonical form table side-by-side with Trino translation: (a) ORDER BY ... WHERE ROWNUM — INVALID Oracle (parse error ORA-00933); (b) WHERE ROWNUM ... ORDER BY — VALID syntax but SEMANTICALLY WRONG (unspecified N rows then sorted); (c) inline-view-wrap CANONICAL Oracle 11g top-N; (d) FETCH FIRST N ROWS ONLY CANONICAL Oracle 12c+; (e) two-level-inline-view CANONICAL Oracle 11g pagination; (f) OFFSET ... FETCH NEXT CANONICAL Oracle 12c+ pagination; (g) keyset pagination — best for deep pages, translates 1:1 to Trino LIMIT. DO-NOT-WRITE block banning: (i) malformed `ORDER BY ... WHERE ROWNUM` in migration audits (invalid Oracle SQL labeled as Oracle); (ii) `WHERE ROWNUM <= 100 ORDER BY ...` labeled as 'Oracle top-N' (it isn't; flag as a likely legacy bug); (iii) SQL Server `SELECT TOP N` as Oracle (wrong dialect); (iv) `WHERE ROWNUM = N` for N>1 (NEVER returns a row in Oracle — assignment-skip behavior; only ROWNUM=1 works on a bare table). Trino destination table mapping 5 intent rows to Trino 467 LIMIT/OFFSET/row_number() forms. Closes with the explanation of why Trino's LIMIT is safe (applies after ORDER BY by language definition; no Oracle-style assignment-skip trap) and cross-refs to Resource 23 (no QUALIFY in Trino 467) and Resource 28 (pagination patterns on big Iceberg tables).
